texts.preamble: Juggi Lal And Another vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2019 Author: Sunita Agarwal Bench: Sunita Agarwal
texts.arguments: Counsel for Revisionist :- Ram Kishor Gupta Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J. Heard learned counsel for the revisionists and learned A.G.A. The present revision has been filed under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C seeking to challenge the judgment and order dated 2.2.1996 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hamirpur in Criminal Case no.576 of 1994 as also judgment and order dated 31.7.1999 passed by second Additional Sessions Judge, Hamirpur in Criminal Appeal No.4 of 1996 whereby the revisionists have been convicted for an offence under section 7(1), read with Section 2( i,a) (a) (m) read with Section-16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for six months of rigorous imprisonment with Rs.1000/- fine each. Submission of learned counsel for the revisionists is that the revisionists have been convicted on the allegations of adulteration in ice-cream which has been reported in the Food laboratory report as of Juggi Lal And Another vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46107093/ 1 sugar content being found less than 10 % as per standards. The said report cannot be made basis for conviction of the revisionists for the reason that the sample was collected on 24.5.1985 and though was sent to the laboratory on 25.5.1985 but the report was obtained on 3.7.1985. The criminal complaint was lodged on 19.6.1986 and the notice was sent to the revisionist thereafter. As a result of delay in taking cognizance on the report, the submissions are two folds, firstly that the laboratory report was obtained after a period of two months and it is not known as to when the sample was examined by the experts. The chemical property of sugar candy is bound to change within a period of two months. The report of laboratory thereafter could not be believed to convict the revisionists. The second submission is that section 13(2) provides opportunity to the revisionists to get an independent analysis of the sample after receipt of the laboratory report which has to be sent within a period of 7 days after receipt of the report of public analyst. The said opportunity as provided in sub-Section (2) of Section 13 has thus been taken away as after a period of one year there remain no purpose for getting an independent report. No objection could be taken to the said submission of learned counsel for the revisionists by the learned A.G.A. The Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of UP reported in AIR 2019 SC 4351 has held that the requirement of Section 13(2) of the Food and Adulteration Act to send the report after institution of prosecution against the person within time prescribed under Rule 9B of Rules, 1955 is mandatory and substantial compliance of the said provision is needed to sustain the conviction.
